question: After the authorization blocker is fixed, should Microsoft Teams adopt this full multi-account configuration as a supported public feature?
rationale: The patch adds a broad public channel configuration, setup, authentication, and state contract; implementation correctness alone cannot establish maintainer product sponsorship.

options.title: Sponsor after repair
options.body: Accept the full multi-account contract after account-scoped authorization and upgrade checks pass.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Land bot identity and routing first while deferring advanced Graph, setup, and per-account policy behavior.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Retain the current single-bot Teams contract until maintainers choose to expand the product surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair
recommendation.body: Accept the full multi-account contract after account-scoped authorization and upgrade checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans the Teams channel and the shared account/default compatibility helpers central to the product choice.
